requirements.requirement: Core-dump payloads are disabled for processes run by local service accounts on node1, including after restart.
requirements.summary: The system-manager default became zero, a controlled systemd-resolve-account crash inherited soft and hard limits of zero and generated no payload, and the same behavior was observed after reboot. The final audit found zero soft and hard limits on all four running local-service-account processes.

requirements.requirement: Normal crash logging remains operational when a local-service-account process crashes.
requirements.summary: Controlled SIGSEGV probes produced journal records containing PID, UID, signal, unit, and failure metadata while explicitly reporting that no coredump payload was generated. Journald and the coredump socket remained active before and after reboot.

overall_summary: Both material outcomes are satisfied with direct pre- and post-reboot behavioral evidence. The mandatory node-restart protocol is complete: it records a healthy pre-restart state, acknowledged reboot scheduling, a changed boot identity independently confirmed by lifecycle observations, and recovered services, journal data, policy, package health, and zero failed units. Hygiene was strong aside from one fully cleaned, low-risk malformed probe.
limitations: The controlled crash behavior was exercised with one representative local service account, systemd-resolve; the final audit covered all four currently running local-service-account service processes but did not individually exercise dormant accounts or non-systemd launch paths.

Any journal record left by the malformed initial probe was not separately inventoried, although its transient unit state and temporary file were cleaned and no failed-unit or temporary-file residue appears in the final lifecycle snapshot.

operational_hygiene.summary: The retained configuration, manager re-execution, successful bounded crash probes, and reboot all had clear task or mandatory restart-evidence roles. One unnecessary mutation occurred: cmd-73ca7e3578d64d69 launched a malformed transient probe whose quoting error prevented the intended crash, so it contributed no useful result. Its temporary output was removed and transient state reset in the same command; final snapshots show no probe file or failed unit. Package health remained intact, and socket differences were only post-reboot PID churn.
